notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.49_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.49.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.49.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

You choose how sharp your camera and shared screen look now, and a call can
move from one of your devices to another.

### Added

- **Choose how good your camera and shared screen look.** Settings has a
  new Video quality section with four levels for each — Highest, High,
  Balanced and Light — and Automatic, which is the default. Highest sends
  your camera at 1080p and a shared screen at up to 4K, so small text in a
  shared document stays readable. Light is for a slow connection: 360p for
  the camera, 720p at a few frames a second for a screen. Until now there
  was no choice — the camera was always 720p and a screen always 1080p at
  15 frames a second. That is still what Automatic sends until it knows
  more about your machine and your connection.
- **Check whether your machine can handle the highest quality.** The
  Video quality section can test this machine: it encodes a few seconds of
  test picture at each level, with the camera off, and says which levels it
  kept up with, whether it has a hardware video encoder, and which
  processor and graphics card it checked. Automatic never goes above what
  the check found.
- **Tell Ruze your upload speed and it shares it out fairly.** There is no
  server in the middle of a call, so your picture goes to each person
  separately, and four people watching uses four times the upload. Enter
  the upload figure from any speed test and Automatic picks a size that
  fits as people join and leave. A level you chose yourself keeps its size
  but is held to what your connection can carry.
- **Move a call between your devices.** Joining a live channel you are
  already in on another device — your phone, say — now asks first: move
  the call here, which hangs up the other device and tells it why, or join
  on both. Until now the second device simply joined as well, and two
  devices in one room near each other hear each other.
- **See who is on a phone.** Somebody in a live channel from their phone
  has a phone beside their name, in the room list and on their tile in the
  call. Somebody in a room on two devices shows on both, each marked, so
  you can tell which is which.

### Fixed

- **Your own devices are not other people.** With a call open on your
  computer, your phone joining it was announced to you by name, as if
  somebody had arrived — and when you were ringing a friend, it counted as
  them picking up, so the ringing stopped though nobody had answered. Your
  own devices are now left out of both.
